findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects resource names as IDs via findByType on the Groups type
findings.body: In the V2 override, the granted IDs are added using groupResource.getId() (the Resource UUID), but the caller expects group IDs (the V1 implementation used resource name suffix). Group resources in V2 are typically named after the group id via the 'all-groups' type resource, so the stored value is the Resource entity id, not the group id. Callers (UserPermissions/UsersResource count and search) pass these to session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) and getUsersCount, which expect group model ids; the result will silently match no groups, so non-admin users with group-based VIEW_MEMBERS will see no members.

findings.title: hasPermission looks up resources by groupId as a resource name, but group resources are named by group id differently and falls back to type resource incorrectly
findings.body: resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) is used to find the group's resource, yet the 'all-groups' fallback uses getResourceTypeResource(...) and then checks policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). If the type resource is null (schema not initialized for the realm), resource.getScopes() / evaluatePermission will throw NPE at line 152 because resource is dereferenced without a null check on the fallback path.

findings.title: canViewMembers/canManageMembers in V2 skip the group-independent MANAGE/VIEW fallback semantics and ignore user-level path
findings.body: canViewMembers(group) only checks VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the group or all-groups resource. The V1 contract and the Javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator say a caller with MANAGE on the group should also view members; V2 canManageMembership checks MANAGE but canViewMembers does not, so behavior is inconsistent with the documented interface.

findings.title: canViewByGroup now calls groups().canViewMembers, changing V1 semantics and recursion through hierarchy
findings.body: canViewByGroup previously used getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) which returned true for users with view-users roles and checked VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS. It now delegates to canViewMembers, which itself returns true when root.users().canView(), causing redundant evaluation per group for every user in the stream filter, a performance regression on large user searches (each user triggers permission evaluation across its whole group hierarchy).

findings.title: canManage/canView/canMapRoles pass group-check results but canMapRoles in V2 now ignores MAP_ROLES semantics for group members
findings.body: canMapRoles in V2 now grants access when the user has MANAGE on the user or manage-members on a group, and the MAP_ROLES scope check is combined with MANAGE in a single OR. This broadens who can map roles compared to the previous MAP_ROLES-only check, a security-relevant permission widening that is not covered by any test in the PR.

findings.title: Inconsistent use of group.getId() vs resource names for group lookup in canView/canManage
findings.body: hasPermission(group.getId(), ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Group resources in this PR are created by the schema with the group id as name (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource), but GroupPermissions (V1) uses a 'group.resource.' prefix; any V2 group resource not yet created will fall through to the all-groups check and may grant access via the type-level permission without a per-group resource, which is intended but untested for the view path.

findings.title: No test covers view of group members through GroupResource.getMembers or getSubGroups filtering
findings.body: The new group-resource tests cover update/create/view listing, but never verify that a user with VIEW_MEMBERS can list members via /groups/{id}/members or that subgroup filtering in GroupResource.getSubGroups honours per-group view permissions after the canView(g) change. The regression risk from the removed canViewGlobal shortcut is untested.

findings.title: getOrCreateResource switch without a default for null resourceType handled inconsistently
findings.body: The switch on resourceType will throw NullPointerException if resourceType is null (switch on a null String), instead of the explicit IllegalStateException used for unknown types. Callers passing a null type from a malformed request will get a 500 instead of a validation error.
